description.value: Investigation of gray matter volume differences between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, and gray matter recovery during the first 14 days of abstinence.

spans.text: To clarify the possibility of early recovery, we investigated volumetric brain changes within the first 2 weeks of abstinence.

value: On the first day of abstinence, alcohol-dependent patients had a significantly smaller GM/TIV ratio and a significantly higher CSF/TIV ratio than healthy controls, whereas WM/TIV did not differ significantly. No gender-by-diagnosis interaction was found.

spans.text: All patients were scanned within 24 hours after the last alcohol consumption, and at this time point, the comparison of the whole-brain volumes in patients and healthy controls revealed significantly smaller GM/TIV ratio and higher CSF/TIV ratio in alcoholic patients, while WM/TIV ratio showed no significant difference.
